The proxy is double-encoding the JSON. The issue: JS sends `dataForRemote` as an object inside the POST body. The proxy reads `dataForRemote` and calls `json_encode($decoded["dataForRemote"])` to re-serialize it. Then it POSTs that to ES.

But wait — the direct browser flow worked (search returned 200 with 6 hits). So the direct mode is fine. The proxy mode has a double-encoding issue. Let me look at how the proxy constructs the remote data.

Actually the error is `[match_all] query malformed, no start_object after query name`. This means the dataForRemote got double-encoded. Let me check: when JS sends `dataForRemote: {"size":1,"query":{...}}`, the proxy does `json_encode($decoded["dataForRemote"])` which turns it into a string `{"size":1,...}`. Then when the proxy sends that to ES via curl, it should be a valid body.

But the error suggests the body sent to ES was something like `"{\"size\":1...}"` (a JSON string) rather than `{"size":1...}`. Let me look at the proxy's curl code to see how it sends the body.
